issues.detail: Example 1 only describes the setup in prose and refers back to the earlier config rather than showing a complete runnable demonstration, and Example 2 is a single short fix.

scenarios.name: fix-invalid-contains-condition
scenarios.rationale: Both explain that Gatus has no 'contains' operator and replace the condition with '[BODY] == pat(*Documentation*)', but B explicitly tells the user to look for the 'Monitored ... success=true' log lines as the rubric requires, whereas A expects 'Listening on :8080' and never mentions the Monitored lines.

scenarios.name: multi-protocol-monitoring-config
scenarios.rationale: Both responses use the right conditions, DNS block, tcp URL, slack provider with ${VAR} expansion, and per-endpoint alerts; A adds slightly more run detail (sqlite storage, health checks), while B has a minor extra (DNS answer assertion tip) and a less current image name, so they are nearly equal.

scenarios.name: persistent-history-docker-compose-deploy
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely: ghcr.io/twin/gatus:stable, config.yaml mounted read-only at /config/config.yaml, sqlite at /data/gatus.db on a named volume, a note that memory storage resets on restart, ${VAR} secrets, and curl checks of /health and /api/v1/endpoints/statuses; B has good persistence and health checks but uses the twinproduction/gatus:latest image, mounts a ./config directory rather than config.yaml itself, and never says memory storage loses history.
